title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 182-184, Longue Marche continuation, c. 1981). An 'L-group' is a discrete group Pi equipped with an 'L-structure': a distinguished family of conjugacy classes of (pro)cyclic 'loop' subgroups (lacets), together with orientation data. The model is the orbifold fundamental group pi_1(X, d, a). Here X is an oriented surface of finite type and d is a positive divisor with finite support and multiplicities in N*, giving cone points of prescribed orders. The base point a lies in X minus supp d. The L-structure comes from the classes of small loops around punctures and cone points.

The previous page asks for a 'good general statement' relating the 2-category of L-groups to the 2-category of such weighted surfaces. It observes that the converse direction (every L-group arises in this way) seems deep, essentially equivalent to finite subgroups of Teichmueller groups having fixed points. The idea is that, apart from a few trivial cases, an L-group Pi should be isomorphic to pi_1(X; G, a), the fundamental group of the quotient orbifold of a surface X by a finite group G acting with an orientation character.

This page adds three points.
(1) Faithfulness of the G-action should be expressible intrinsically in Pi: the centralizer of every finite-index subgroup of Pi is {e}. This is the condition of trivial virtual centralizers, which excludes finite normal subgroups and virtual centers.
(2) This should give an intrinsic, topological description of the L-groups having this extra property. These are essentially the L-groups of hyperbolic 2-orbifolds, i.e. Fuchsian / NEC groups with peripheral structure.
(3) A further gluing ('recollement') step treats the general case. It would use certain extensions of such L-groups by finite groups, which corresponds to non-faithful actions with finite kernel.
Finally, the 'L-Galois topoi' attached to L-groups should be related to Pi, by paraphrasing the theory of Galois topoi attached to discrete groups / groups with loops. This would give the topos-theoretic counterpart of the equivalence between L-groups and orbifold surfaces.

The purpose is to set up a purely algebraic category (L-groups) equivalent to the category of 2-orbifolds of finite type. The next page proposes it as the right framework for general Teichmueller groups, e.g. the L-structure on PSL(2,Z) and the 'every direct L-automorphism is inner' property.
errors: No error in the stated criterion. If G acts with finite kernel K, then K is a finite normal subgroup. Its centralizer C(K) has finite index, and K is contained in the centralizer of C(K). So K is nontrivial exactly when some finite-index subgroup has nontrivial centralizer.

Conversely, for hyperbolic orbifolds, finite-index subgroups are non-elementary Fuchsian groups, so their centralizers are trivial. The excluded 'trivial cases' (Euclidean/spherical orbifolds, tori, etc.) indeed violate the condition or need separate treatment.

The sufficiency direction ('every L-group with this property is an orbifold group') is only conjectural here and requires the deep input acknowledged on the previous page (Nielsen realization / recognition of virtual surface groups).

ideas.what: Faithfulness of the finite group action on the surface is equivalent to the orbifold group having trivial centralizers of all finite-index subgroups (no nontrivial finite normal subgroups / virtual center)
ideas.modern_name: Trivial virtual centralizers; finite normal subgroups of Fuchsian/NEC groups; effective vs ineffective orbifolds
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in the theory of Fuchsian and planar discontinuous groups (Zieschang et al.)

ideas.what: Intrinsic algebraic characterization of orbifold fundamental groups of surfaces of finite type with peripheral (loop) structure
ideas.modern_name: Recognition of Fuchsian groups / virtual PD2 pairs as 2-orbifold groups (group pairs with peripheral structure)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Zieschang; Eckmann-Mueller-Linnell (PD2 groups are surface groups); Kerckhoff (Nielsen realization, 1983)
ideas.where_published: Groups with loops (groupes à lacets) appear in La Longue Marche (1981, circulated); this L-group variant appears unpublished

ideas.what: Treat non-faithful actions via extensions of 'good' L-groups by finite groups (recollement)
ideas.modern_name: Finite extensions / gerbes over orbifolds (non-effective orbifolds)

ideas.what: L-Galois topoi associated to L-groups, paralleling Galois topoi of discrete groups / groups with loops
ideas.modern_name: Classifying topos of the orbifold with peripheral (boundary) structure; étale topos of a 2-orbifold / stacky curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Topos-theoretic Galois theory (SGA 1/SGA 4, Moerdijk on étendues/orbifolds)

missed.claim: Programme for an equivalence between the 2-category of L-groups (with the trivial-virtual-centralizer condition) and the 2-category of effective hyperbolic 2-orbifolds of finite type. It is to be completed by a gluing step for finite extensions and by a topos-theoretic version ('topos L-galoisiens'). The topos part was never written up.
missed.quote: il faudrait faire le lien avec les "topos L-galoisiens" associés, en paraphrasant les développements correspondants sur les topos galoisiens
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The group-theoretic side is largely covered by later results (Kerckhoff, recognition of Fuchsian groups). A clean 2-categorical statement with peripheral structure, plus its topos version, would still be a tidy foundation for anabelian treatments of orbifold curves and Teichmueller groupoids. It is not a missing theorem, however.

deep.surprise_reason: A sensible but routine-level remark: the 'faithful action iff trivial centralizers of finite-index subgroups' criterion is standard for Fuchsian/NEC groups. The broader programme (L-groups as the setting for Teichmueller groups) is consistent with known Longue Marche themes, and the topos part is only a sketched intention.
transcription_corrections: 'une description intrinsèque, en termes topologiques, les L-groupes' should read 'des L-groupes'.
Final line likely reads 'associés aux groupes à lacets' (not 'groupes discrets'); the line before may read 'topos galoisiens etc.'
'recollement' is plausible for the uncertain word.
